# ShutdownRelay

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Core/ShutdownRelay.cs#L19)

The Unity half of the platform's remote lifecycle protocol. The headset management service
broadcasts ACTION_SHUTDOWN to close an app remotely and ACTION_GET_RUNNING_APPS to find out
what is running; this relay answers both, and announces the app once it is actually on screen.
The Java side (com.cievr.shutdown.AppEvents) reaches Unity through
UnityPlayer.UnitySendMessage, which addresses a GameObject by name - so this component lives on
its own object called [`ObjectName`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/ShutdownRelay#objectname) and survives scene loads. [`VRCore`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/VRCore)
creates it and hangs the scene's module teardown off [`ShutdownRequested`](/api/vrframework-core-runtime/ShutdownRelay#shutdownrequested), so a
remote close runs the same cleanup a normal scene teardown does before the app quits.
Off Android - and in the editor - the native calls compile out and this is an inert object:
the broadcasts it answers can only arrive on a device.

```csharp

public class ShutdownRelay : MonoBehaviour
```

### OnShutdownRequested(string) {#onshutdownrequested-string}

Called by AppEvents when ACTION_SHUTDOWN arrives. Runs teardown, acknowledges, then quits.
The acknowledgement is sent before [`Quit()`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Application.Quit.html) so the broadcast leaves
the process while there still is one.

## Events

### ShutdownRequested {#shutdownrequested}

Raised when the platform asks the app to close, before the acknowledgement goes back.
Subscribers do their teardown synchronously - saving progress, closing connections,
releasing hardware - because the process is torn down right after.

```csharp
public event Action ShutdownRequested
```

**Returns** [`Action`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.action)
